name: Heat Loss Calculator - Pipe & Tank Insulation
description: Calculate heat loss from insulated or uninsulated pipes and tanks to ambient air, with economic insulation thickness.

seo.title: Pipe Heat Loss Calculator - Insulation
seo.description: Calculate heat loss from pipes, tanks, and vessels with or without insulation. Estimate energy savings from adding insulation.

formula.explanation: Cylindrical heat loss with insulation. R_total = R_outside + R_insulation. R_outside = 1/(hπD), R_insulation = ln((D+2t)/D)/(2πk). h = outside convection coefficient.

content.introduction: Calculate conductive and convective heat loss from insulated or bare pipes and cylindrical equipment. Essential for energy audits, insulation specification, and tracing/heat-up calculations.

example.description: 114mm pipe at 150°C with 50mm mineral wool insulation, 100m long: ~4.7 kW heat loss.

faq.q: What is a typical insulation k-value?
faq.a: Mineral wool: 0.035-0.045; polyurethane foam: 0.022-0.030; calcium silicate: 0.055-0.070; fiberglass: 0.034-0.045 W/mK.

faq.q: How much energy does insulation save?
faq.a: Uninsulated 150°C pipes lose ~20x more heat than well-insulated ones. Insulation typically pays back in under a year on hot pipes.
